archetype.name: Pocket Passer (downfield)
archetype.definition: A stationary, run-game-dependent passer whose value comes from throws 10+ yards past the line rather than from his legs or the quick game.

report.headline: The downfield efficiency is real, but blowout leads and hot samples flatter it.
report.take:
Penix took over in Week 3 of a run-first offense: Atlanta passes far less than situations predict (-8.3 pass rate over expected, 29th) and leans on a run game ranked 3rd in EPA. His job is to punish defenses that crowd the box, and he does. He ranks 5th in yards per attempt (8.58) and 5th in adjusted net yards per dropback (9.03). He contributes nothing as a runner, with 5 rushing yards and three scrambles that all lost value.

The value is concentrated almost entirely downfield. Throws of 10+ air yards have added 34.8 EPA, while everything under 10 yards has added -4.2. The drag is the screen and swing game: passes behind the line have cost -16.1 EPA, and Bijan Robinson's targets are at -0.409 per target. Drake London (25.9 EPA) and Kyle Pitts (0.834 per target) are where the offense lives. The other notable change is accuracy. His bad-throw rate is 9.1%, down 13.4 points from last year, and his time to throw dropped from 2.79 to 2.54. That points to a quicker, cleaner process, not just better luck.

The headline efficiency hides a lot. When leading by 9+ he has added 21.2 EPA, which is more than all of his dropbacks combined (15.5). In one-score games his EPA per play is exactly 0. Much of the 0.151 EPA per dropback was built in the routs of Green Bay and New Orleans. The deep numbers (1.487 EPA on 11 attempts) and five red-zone TDs on 40.9% completions are small, hot samples. His CPOE (-0.45, 27th) is better than his career norm of roughly -4 but still below average.

The last two games show the counter-pressure. Baltimore pressured him 21.6% of the time and his bad-throw rate jumped to 19.4%. Chicago sacked him five times and forced a lost fumble, producing -9.8 EPA even though he threw 3 TDs. He is rarely pressured (9.6%, lowest among 37 qualifiers), yet he takes sacks on 36.4% of pressures, 32nd of 37. That is a real flaw, and it is worse than his career rate of about a quarter. Over his last three games, the sack rate has risen to 9.6% and EPA per dropback has fallen to 0.09. He is a useful, above-average passer in this system, not the top-five one his yards-per-attempt suggests.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep throws drive everything
strengths.body: Throws beyond 10 air yards carry his entire value, at nearly 0.9 EPA per attempt with a positive CPOE. The run game's success opens these windows, and London and Pitts win in them. The intermediate rate (0.66 on 28 attempts) is the more trustworthy piece. The deep rate will cool.

strengths.title: Cleaner ball placement than his history
strengths.body: His bad-throw rate has fallen from 22.5% (59th of 63 last year) to 9.1%, alongside a quicker release. Two straight seasons near the bottom argue for some caution. Still, the drop is large enough, and paired with a clear process change, that part of it should stick.

strengths.title: Moving the sticks on third down
strengths.body: On third down he has posted 0.472 EPA per play and a 45.9% conversion rate, facing an average of 7.7 yards to go. Four of his TDs came there. With 37 plays it is a meaningful hint, though not yet a fact.

concerns.title: Sacks when the pocket does break
concerns.body: He is the least-pressured qualifier, yet among the worst at avoiding sacks once pressure arrives. It isn't the cost of scrambling, since he barely scrambles and those plays have been negative. It looks like holding the ball for the downfield read. Chicago's five sacks and fumble show how fast this erases a game.

concerns.title: Efficiency built in blowouts
concerns.body: Leading by 9+, he has produced more EPA than across all his dropbacks. In one-score games his EPA is flat at 0, and trailing by 9+ it is negative. The routs of Green Bay and New Orleans carry the season line. Competitive games are a more honest read of him.

concerns.title: Dead weight behind the line
concerns.body: Throws behind the line of scrimmage have completed at 59.3% with a -21.9 CPOE, costing more EPA than his deep shots have added. Robinson's targets are negative. Part of this is scheme and execution around him, not just the QB, but it is a drag on every drive that leans on it.

trend.note: His passing EPA went 9.5, 10.6, 7.6, then -9.8 against Chicago. Over the last three games, EPA per dropback (0.09) and CPOE (-3.5) have slid while the sack rate has climbed. Fantasy points rose anyway on Week 6's three TDs, which masks the decline.

nextGame.headline: Run game stalls against SF, but Bosa's absence eases pressure
nextGame.body:
San Francisco's defense is built to take away exactly what Atlanta leans on. It ranks 2nd against the run by EPA and 1st at preventing explosive runs. That pushes the game onto Penix, and as a 3.5-point home underdog against the league's top passing offense, he may be throwing from behind. His trailing splits are poor. The pass defense is softer: 14th in EPA and 21st on short throws. It is stingy on explosive passes (4th), though, which is where Penix makes his living.

Availability tilts things his way. Nick Bosa (64% of snaps) is out, removing the rusher most likely to expose his sack habit, and the 49ers already rank only 15th in hit rate. Starting safety Marques Sigle (88% of snaps) is also out, thinning the coverage behind the intermediate and deep throws Penix depends on. Atlanta lists no offensive injuries. On the other side, Deebo Samuel is out, Mike Evans is doubtful and Christian Kirk is on IR, which may slow the shootout pace somewhat.

keyMatchups.title: Run game into a wall
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's 3rd-ranked rushing offense meets the 2nd-ranked run defense. If early downs fail, Penix faces more obvious passing downs, where his sack rate becomes a live risk.

keyMatchups.title: London against a neutral WR1 matchup
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco has let WR1s score slightly above their averages (21st) and has smothered WR2s. Expect the volume to funnel to London, whose targets carry most of Penix's value. Pitts faces a mid-pack TE1 defense.

keyMatchups.title: Chunk plays without Sigle
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco allows few explosive passes, but losing an 88%-snap safety tests that. Whether Penix can hit 10+ yard throws against a depleted secondary decides whether he clears his recent form.

nextGame.watch: Sacks on pressured dropbacks: without Bosa, a clean game here would suggest Weeks 5-6 were opponent-driven rather than a habit.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is sustainable. Atlanta's line keeps him clean, the run game creates favorable passing windows, and London and Pitts win downfield. A real accuracy gain also seems to have arrived with a quicker release. Several pieces will regress. The deep rate on 11 attempts, five red-zone TDs on 40.9% completions, and efficiency inflated by two routs should all cool. His CPOE is likely to sit near or below average, given a career of roughly -4.

Expect a good-not-great passer: yards per attempt in the high 7s, about 210-255 yards a game, and one to two TDs, in an offense that won't ask him to throw 35 times unless trailing. The sack issue is the variable that decides his floor. If his pressure-to-sack rate drifts back toward his career norm, he stays solidly positive in EPA. If it doesn't, more Chicago-style games follow.
swingFactors: Pressure-to-sack rate regressing toward his career level
Atlanta's run game holding up to keep him in favorable downs
Whether the bad-throw improvement survives tougher defenses

confidence.note: Four starts, with splits on very small samples and two blowouts inflating them, but the career baseline helps frame what's real.
